course.title: Photoshop Intermediate: From Practitioner to Pro
course.subtitle: Professional technique, real color management, and client-ready work.
course.description: The sequel to the intro course. It assumes you can already operate Photoshop non-destructively (layers, masks, selections, Camera Raw, Curves, Smart Objects, basic retouching and compositing) and takes you to a professional standard: luminosity and channel masking, real color management and soft proofing, high-end retouching, commercial compositing, design systems, advanced generative and automation workflows, and multi-shot techniques.

author.name: Ray de la Paz
author.bio: Technical trainer, full-stack developer, and course developer with 30+ years of experience.

prerequisite: The intro course (Photoshop: From First Win to Finished Work) or equivalent comfort with layers, masks, selections, Camera Raw, Curves, Smart Objects, and basic compositing.

structure.note: No beginner on-ramp module. The course opens on real technique. Core ideas from the intro (non-destructive editing, the layer stack, masks-as-grayscale, selections) return at professional depth. Setup and color management are folded into a Before You Start section and Module 2, not a standalone module.

modules.title: Module 1 — Advanced Selection & Masking
modules.deliverable: A flawless cutout of a hard subject (wispy hair, glass, foliage) on a new background.
modules.description: Selections and masks driven by the image's own tones and channels, not just the brush.

lessons.title: Select & Mask Mastery: The Hard Cutout

modules.title: Module 2 — Color & Tone, Deep
modules.deliverable: A cinematic grade plus a print-ready, soft-proofed export.
modules.description: Color management done right, then grading with Curves, gradient maps, and LUTs.

lessons.title: Grading with Curves, Gradient Maps & LUTs

modules.title: Module 3 — High-End Retouching
modules.description: The full professional skin and portrait workflow, kept natural.

modules.title: Module 4 — Commercial Compositing
modules.deliverable: An advertising-style key visual from three or more elements.
modules.description: Believable light direction, shadows, reflections, atmosphere, and scale.

modules.title: Module 5 — Design Systems & Type
modules.deliverable: A small campaign (poster + matched social set) from one master file.
modules.description: Type systems, templates, linked assets, and multi-deliverable output.

modules.title: Module 6 — Generative + Automation, Advanced
modules.deliverable: A data-driven batch (e.g. 20 product cards) plus a generative-assisted composite.
modules.description: Generative tools for real production, and automation from Actions to scripting.

modules.title: Module 7 — Multi-Shot Techniques
modules.deliverable: A merged panorama or focus-stacked image, and a short animated social asset.
modules.description: Bonus module: combining many frames into one, plus timeline animation.

modules.title: Module 8 — Capstone
modules.deliverable: A self-directed professional brief with a written case study, presented.
modules.description: Plan, execute, and present a client-shaped deliverable end to end.

modules.title: ↔ Recipes II
modules.description: "How do I luminosity-mask a sky?" "How do I match two images' color?" "How do I set up a data merge?" Short answers for the harder tasks, each linking to the module that teaches it in depth.

visualsPolicy.note: Same approach as the intro. Hand-built SVG panel/dialog diagrams and process illustrations, theme-aware Mermaid, and real before/after photos where the connected Adobe tools can produce the edit (tonal/color grades, background removal, generative expand, soft-proof color shifts). Techniques the connector cannot reproduce (luminosity/channel masking, frequency separation, dodge & burn, multi-image compositing) are taught with labeled SVG process diagrams and stand-ins.
